key_insight: FACTR 2 shows that low-cost robot arms can learn useful external force sensing without dedicated force sensors. Its NEXT method estimates external joint torques from short free-motion data, enabling force-aware manipulation and better policy learning.
problem_solved: Many commodity robot arms lack force/torque sensors, making contact-rich tasks and force-feedback teleoperation difficult and expensive. This paper addresses the gap by providing a fast, data-driven way to recover force information from ordinary robot hardware.
method: Train Neural External Torque Estimation (NEXT) from only 10 minutes of free-motion robot data.
Use the learned model to estimate external joint torques without any dedicated force sensors.
Apply the estimated force signals for force-feedback teleoperation and to improve learning for manipulation policies.
impact: This matters because it brings force sensing to inexpensive robot arms, lowering hardware cost and setup complexity. For AI/ML practitioners, it enables better contact-rich policy learning and more capable real-world robotic systems with minimal additional instrumentation.

paper_title: FACTR 2: Learning External Force Sensing for Commodity Robot Arms Improves Policy Learning
paper_authors: Steven Oh, Jason Jingzhou Liu, Tony Tao, Philip Han, Kenneth Shaw
